Indicator 7a tracks the pass rate of the primary school leaving exam (folkeskolens afgangseksamen) among youth in the [[adhd-udredningspopulation|ADHD-udredningspopulation]] compared to the [[baggrundspopulationen-2023|Baggrundspopulationen 2023]] across Danish regions. The data reveals a persistent and significant educational gap, with the ADHD assessment population consistently trailing the background population by 25 to 30 percentage points in both 2023 and 2024 [^src1][^src2].

In 2023, the national pass rate for the ADHD population was 55%, compared to 86% for the background population [^src1]. [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]] was the clear leader, achieving a 64% pass rate, while [[region-sjaelland|Region Sjælland]] was the lowest performer at 50% [^src1]. The remaining regions—[[region-syddanmark|Region Syddanmark]] (54%), [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]] (52%), and [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]] (53%)—clustered closely around the national average [^src1].

By 2024, the national pass rate for the ADHD population dipped slightly to 53%, while the background population's rate fell to 84% [^src2]. [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]] maintained its position as the leader with a 63% pass rate [^src2]. However, the bottom of the ranking shifted: [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]] and [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]] both dropped to 47%, becoming the new lowest performers [^src2]. Meanwhile, [[region-sjaelland|Region Sjælland]] saw a marginal improvement to 51%, and [[region-syddanmark|Region Syddanmark]] remained stable at 53% [^src2].

Despite these minor regional fluctuations, the overarching trend is one of stagnation. No region has managed to close the 25–30 percentage point deficit between the ADHD assessment population and their peers in the background population [^src1][^src2]. The structural disadvantage faced by youth in the ADHD assessment population remains entrenched across all geographical areas [^src1][^src2].
